title: Color, Shape, and Line
summary: Students learn beginner-friendly English for color, palette, shape, line, silhouette, and overall visual impression so they can describe a look, sketch, or fashion figure respectfully and clearly.
essential_question: How can I describe what a fashion look looks like visually in simple English?
professional_context: Week 6 connects English to early fashion drawing, creativity-lab observation, look description, and beginner portfolio-style language. Students move from naming garments and figure parts to describing visual elements such as color palette, silhouette, lines, shape, and overall impression.
language_focus: adjective order in simple garment phrases
grammar_focus: adjective order in phrases such as a long black dress and a soft pink blouse
singular and plural agreement in The dress is ... and The pants are ...
teacher_preparation: Preview the opener multi-look board, the color and palette board, the shape-line-silhouette board, the reading gallery, and the four-look gallery before class.
Prepare visible sentence frames for The color is ..., The palette is ..., The silhouette is ..., The lines are ..., The look has ..., and I like the ... because ....
Review Week 6 correction targets, especially adjective order, plural agreement with pants and shorts, and The color palette is ... .
Decide whether students will choose their look for the main writing task from a projected gallery, printed cards, or a future app gallery.
Keep the Week 6 listening audio or teacher read-aloud fallback aligned to the same image A-D gallery used in listening, writing, and speaking.
student_deliverables: Completion of the Week 6 visual opener.
Completion of the main color and palette matching set.
Completion of the main shape-line-silhouette matching set.
Reading-comprehension responses matching three look descriptions to image A, B, or C and answering detail questions.
Listening-comprehension responses identifying four looks from one audio clip.
Completion of adjective-order and look-description phrase-practice frames.
A scaffolded Color and Shape Look Description with 6 required sentence-frame lines and 1 optional challenge sentence.
One corrected Week 6 sentence saved after review.
A short teacher-observed oral look description using prepared sentence frames.
